content.title: About
content.content: Grilled salmon retains a tender, smoky flavor while offering a rich nutritional profile. It is a popular choice for healthy eating because the fish provides high‑quality protein, beneficial fatty acids, and a variety of vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Salmon is one of the few fish that contains significant amounts of the omega‑3 fatty acids EPA and DHA.
Wild salmon generally contains more nutrients than farm‑raised salmon.
Grilling helps preserve a large portion of vitamin D, which is important for bones and immunity.
Salmon can change the color of its flesh depending on its diet; those that eat krill have a brighter orange hue.
In Japan, grilled salmon is often served with soy sauce and lemon to highlight its natural taste.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Omega‑3s support cardiovascular health, lower triglyceride levels, and have anti‑inflammatory effects.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Salmon protein is easily digestible and essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Vitamin D
items.content: Salmon is one of the best dietary sources of vitamin D, crucial for bone health and immune function.

items.title: Vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 supports the nervous system and participates in red blood cell formation.

items.title: Selenium
items.content: Selenium acts as a powerful antioxidant, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Some salmon may contain traces of mercury or polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs); moderate consumption is advised, especially for children and pregnant women.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Certain individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Overcooking
items.content: Excessive grilling can create harmful compounds such as acrylamide, so cook salmon until golden but not dry.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve grilled salmon hot, sliced into portions. It pairs well with lemon, herbs, olive oil, or soy sauce. Great alongside vegetable sides, quinoa, mashed potatoes, or fresh salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh salmon fillets in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C, wrapped in film or an airtight container, for up to 2 days. Frozen salmon retains quality for up to 3 months at –18 °C. Thaw in the fridge before cooking and pat dry.
